# Results — Study 77 (Golden-Mean) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One test: swings are
identified on daily closes using a 60-bar lookback and a 5%-minimum swing size; the
Fibonacci retracement levels (38.2%, 50%, 61.8%) within each swing are checked for
touches over the following 40 calendar days; the 5-day forward return is measured
from the first touch in the predicted bounce direction. The identical procedure is
run on **placebo levels** — randomly-placed levels within the same swing range — to
isolate any *Fibonacci-specific* effect from generic mean reversion. Daily data from
Yahoo Finance. As-of **2026-06-12**. Pooled across 6 instruments: **n = 11,115
Fibonacci touches**.*

## The honest test — Fibonacci levels vs placebo, gross (cost = 0)

A **placebo** arm runs the *identical* event-study pipeline with randomly-placed
levels at the same position within the swing range. If Fibonacci is magic, the
Fibonacci arm must *beat* the placebo arm — touching a Fibonacci level must produce
better forward returns than touching a non-Fibonacci level. Both arms inherit the
same equity drift and mean-reversion base rate; only the *Fibonacci specificity*
separates them.

| Arm | n touches | bounce rate | mean (bps/5-day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Fibonacci (38.2% / 50% / 61.8%)** | 11,115 | 53.3% | **+24.80** | **+2.96** |
| **Placebo (random levels, same swing)** | 10,785 | 53.5% | **+28.78** | **+3.94** |

- **Both arms have positive 5-day forward returns.** This is not evidence of an edge
  — it is the equity risk premium. Stocks drift upward over 5-day windows on average;
  any entry (level-based or random) captures this drift.
- **The Fibonacci arm does NOT beat the placebo.** Fibonacci − Placebo =
  **−3.98 bps** — Fibonacci levels are actually slightly *worse* than random levels.
  The bounce rate is nearly identical (53.3% vs 53.5%). There is no Fibonacci
  specificity.
- **Per-instrument: no tape shows a Fibonacci advantage over placebo.** On 4 of 6
  tickers the placebo beats Fibonacci; on QQQ Fibonacci wins by 3.6 bps. None of
  these differences are statistically meaningful.

| Ticker | Fib mean (bps) | Fib *t* | Plac mean (bps) | Plac *t* | Fib − Plac |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY  | +26.00 | +2.63 | +27.02 | +3.20 | −1.02 |

## Per-Fibonacci-ratio breakdown (pooled, gross)

All three canonical ratios produce similar forward returns — there is nothing special
about 61.8% over 38.2% or 50%, and none of them beat the placebo when compared
within their respective swing.

| Ratio | n touches | bounce rate | mean (bps/5-day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 38.2% | 3,285 | 53.3% | +28.59 | +2.15 |
| 50.0% | 3,763 | 52.5% | +20.28 | +1.74 |
| 61.8% | 4,067 | 54.1% | +25.94 | +2.50 |

## Round numbers vs midpoints (gross, 5-day forward)

Round-number levels ($5/$10/$50/$100 steps near the current price) are tested
separately. The control is the *midpoint* between adjacent round numbers — equally
spaced, but not "round". If round numbers are special, they must beat their
midpoints.

| Arm | n touches | bounce rate | mean (bps/5-day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Round numbers | 16,462 | 49.6% | −7.49 | −1.53 |
| Midpoints (control) | 15,958 | 49.2% | −8.65 | −1.66 |
| Round − Midpoint | — | — | **+1.16** | — |

- Round numbers show **no statistically meaningful advantage** over midpoints
  (+1.16 bps, HAC *t* not computed for the difference — both arms are in the noise).
- Both arms are slightly negative in 5-day return, reflecting the measurement
  convention (approaching from below → expect up; from above → expect down), which
  tends to enter against the prevailing trend.

## Fibonacci cost sweep (net, 5-day forward)

The Fibonacci arm's positive gross return is the equity drift, not Fibonacci
specificity. After any cost the gross advantage over "do nothing" shrinks, but the
Fibonacci-vs-placebo gap remains at roughly −3.98 bps regardless of cost.

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/5-day) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | +24.80 | +2.96 |
| 1.0 bps | +23.80 | +2.84 |
| 5.0 bps | +19.80 | +2.36 |

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Fibonacci levels produce a +24.80 bps 5-day forward return
  (HAC *t* = +2.96) — but so does the placebo (+28.78 bps, *t* = +3.94). The
  Fibonacci arm *underperforms* randomly-placed control levels by **−3.98 bps**,
  with no ticker showing a consistent Fibonacci advantage. The positive returns
  are the equity risk premium, not evidence of Fibonacci magic. There is no
  Fibonacci-specific directional information in the data.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** When the control (placebo) outperforms the signal,
  there is nothing to trade. A long-only entry at any touch would capture some
  equity drift, but so would buying on any random day — the Fibonacci levels add
  no incremental value.
- **Beats random levels? — BUSTED.** Fibonacci levels do not produce more or better
  bounces than randomly-placed levels within the same price swing. The 53% bounce
  rate is slightly below the placebo's 53.5%. Round numbers show a +1.16 bps
  advantage over midpoints — statistical noise.
